title: Redwood data retention demo - Paragon Payments
summary: Product walkthrough focused on data handling and retention controls: logging redaction, PII detection, request storage toggles, KMS integration, and Private/VPC options. Customer concerned about auditability, encryption, and ability to disable storage for sensitive flows. Agreed next steps: send security pack, share demo recording, schedule pilot benchmark with masked PII set.
next_steps: Maya to send Redwood security pack and SOC2 docs by 2026-05-10
Rafael to share short demo recording and console walkthrough link
Customer to provide sample redaction rules and a small PII dataset for pilot by 2026-05-14
action_items: Maya Chen: send security pack + pricing sheet by 2026-05-10
Rafael Ortiz: export console recording + step-by-step guide by 2026-05-08
Priya Singh: share sample PII patterns and example logs by 2026-05-14
Lena Park: confirm legal contact for DPA by 2026-05-12
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-07, 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rafael (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood Prod), Lena (Paragon Head of Security), Omar (CTO), Priya (Lead SRE), Ethan (PM)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll run a quick data retention and logging controls demo today. raf, samir are here to jump into the console and technical bits.
[00:18] Omar: great, thanks. we mostly want to validate whether we can guarantee no retention for specific flows and also how redaction works before we send anything to production.
[00:32] Rafael: totally, we'll show the api toggles, console settings, and the optimize recommendations around caching vs redaction. quick note, some names might be a little off in the transcription.
[00:45] Lena: perfect. our compliance team cares about SOC2, SSO, and KMS. we also need audit logs to show who accessed what and when.
[00:58] Samir: we'll cover audit logs and role-based access. redwood supports SAML SSO and has audit trails per request id and token.
[01:15] Priya: do you have HSM integration? we need customer-managed keys for certain workflows.
[01:22] Rafael: yes, KMS and HSM integrations are supported. we showed a KMS flow earlier this week, i'll highlight key rotation and envelope encryption in a sec.
[01:36] Ethan: quick Q — can we disable request storage per route? some endpoints are highly sensitive.
[01:42] Maya: yes, there are request storage toggles at the route and model level. you can set store: true/false; also ephemeral mode for zero retention of request/response bodies. we'll demo the console switch.
[02:03] [screen share starts] Rafael: ok i'm in the console, navigating to Projects > paragon-payments > routes. here's the route settings panel, see 'Data handling' section: Request storage: enabled, options: store, ephemeral, masked.
[02:24] Rafael: if you pick 'masked' we run server-side PII detection and redact identified spans before storage. rules can be custom regexes or use our ML PII detector.
[02:40] Lena: are those PII detectors running in our VPC or on your hosted side? we need to know where raw text touches.
[02:48] Rafael: good question. for hosted Redwoods the detector runs in the Redwood service; for Private deployments the ML detector can run in your VPC. also, you can configure client-side pre-send redaction.
[03:05] Omar: so for hosted, raw text may leave your infra unless we use Private mode?
[03:11] Maya: correct, hosted routes are processed by redwood infra; if you need full control, Private deployment keeps ingress in your VPC and integrates with your KMS.
[03:25] Priya: can we still get audit logs while keeping ephemeral storage? we need to show requests but not the payload.
[03:32] Rafael: yes — audit logs capture metadata (request id, timestamp, model, token counts, user id) without storing the full payload when ephemeral is enabled. you can also enable hash-only storage where payloads are hashed for dedup but not stored.
[03:53] [05:00] Rafael: switching to the redaction rules page, you can add regex-based rules, toggle ML detector sensitivity, and preview redactions against sample logs. note: the preview is done against a masked copy, not your live production traffic.
[05:25] Lena: is there an approvals workflow for adding redaction rules? our security team wants change audit.
[05:32] Samir: there's RBAC around rule edits; rule changes generate an audit entry and you can enforce a code-review-like approval workflow through our API so changes require an approver.
[05:50] Ethan: if we choose masked storage, can we still run evals and retrain locally? we need sanitized transcripts for internal model testing.
[05:58] Rafael: yes, masked or redacted data can be exported to a secure bucket; you can choose to export only token counts or the sanitized transcript. exports respect retention policies.
[06:15] Lena: what's the retention granularity? per-route, per-org?
[06:20] Rafael: retention policies are hierarchical: org default, project override, route override. you can set retention in days, e.g., 30 days for logs, 365 for embeddings, or indefinite for audit events.
[06:38] Priya: we have a regulation that requires 7 years of certain audit events. can we keep audit events longer than request bodies?
[06:45] Maya: yes, audit events are separate and can be configured for long-term retention; bodies can be ephemeral while audit events remain.
[06:58] [08:00] Omar: what about encryption at rest? full-disk? per-object? customer keys?
[08:07] Rafael: we encrypt at rest by default and support customer-managed KMS keys for object encryption. for Private deployments, you can bring your own HSM. We also support per-object encryption using envelope encryption.
[08:28] Lena: is the access to KMS logs preserved? we need to show key usage to auditors.
[08:33] Samir: yes, KMS access logs and audit trails are accessible; we can map KMS calls into the audit UI and export to your SIEM.
[08:50] [09:30] Rafael: demoing API — you can set the header x-redwood-store: false to bypass storage for single requests; the console toggle sets policy, but headers allow ad-hoc ephemeral calls.
[09:58] Priya: that's useful for on-demand sensitive lookups. is that header enforceable by role?
[10:05] Rafael: enforcement is tied to API tokens and scopes; we can restrict the ability to set store=false to tokens with a specific scope. audit logs will record who used the header.
[10:22] Lena: any rate of false positives with PII detector? we can't redact transaction ids accidentally.
[10:29] Rafael: ML detector has sensitivity levels and a whitelist/blacklist to avoid masking structured IDs; you can add allow-lists for patterns you trust. preview helps validate.
[10:46] [12:00] Maya: let's walk through a sample sensitive flow — payment dispute intake — which must not retain raw PII but needs analytics. raf?
[12:09] Rafael: step 1: set route to ephemeral storage. step 2: enable hashed metadata export & aggregate telemetry to our Optimize pipeline which will capture metrics without raw payloads. step 3: if you want sanitized transcripts, enable masked storage + export to your secure bucket with KMS.
[12:33] Omar: for analytics, will aggregates be accurate if we mask names?
[12:37] Rafael: yes, aggregates like counts, latency, token distribution are unaffected; for entity-level analysis you can export sanitized entity mentions instead of full text.
[12:52] Priya: can we run the PII detector offline against our historical logs? we want to backfill redaction rules.
[12:59] Rafael: you can run our detector as a batch job in Private mode, or we can provide a redaction CLI that runs in your environment.
[13:15] Ethan: where do we configure retention from the API?
[13:20] Rafael: Projects API > PATCH /projects/:id/retention with JSON like {"route_id":..., "retention_days":30, "store": "masked"} — i'll include examples in the follow-up doc.
[13:40] [15:00] Maya: quick security checklist — SOC2 status, SAML SSO, KMS, dedicated hosts, private deployment. lena, is that the main list?
[15:07] Lena: yes plus data residency for EU flows and DPA standard clauses.
[15:14] Samir: for data residency we can region-pin processing; Private deployments allow you to keep traffic in your cloud account.
[15:26] Omar: cost tradeoff question — does ephemeral storage or masking add latency / cost?
[15:33] Rafael: masking adds minimal compute for the detector; ephemeral storage reduces storage costs but may increase egress if you export sanitized copies. Private deployments have infra cost overhead but keep data in your control. we'll run a cost estimate in the pilot.
[15:52] Priya: we'd like a pilot with a 1k/day sample for 2 weeks to measure latency and redaction accuracy.
[16:00] Maya: sounds good. we'll propose scope after sending the security pack.
[16:08] Ethan: any open-source components we should be aware of in the PII detector?
[16:13] Rafael: some components are based on open-source token classifiers but our enterprise offering includes hardened models and QA. we can provide SBOM on request.
[16:27] [18:00] Rafael: demo — show console audit timeline. here you can filter by request id, see who viewed the log, and download redaction diffs.
[18:44] Lena: downloads — who can access these? only admins?
[18:48] Samir: controls are RBAC-driven; you can restrict downloads to specific roles and require SSO approval.
[19:05] [20:00] Maya: quick note on DPA and legal — we have a template and standard clauses; lena if you want we'll loop legal contacts.
[20:12] Lena: yes please, we need to review DPA and incident response SLAs.
[20:20] Maya: noted, we'll include DPA + incident response in the security pack.
[20:33] [22:00] Omar: small technical deep dive — for Private deployments, what's the deployment model? containerized + helm chart?
[22:10] Rafael: yes, we provide a helm chart and a controller, plus an operator for lifecycle. networking uses VPC peering or private link; we provide ops runbook.
[22:29] Priya: do you support air-gapped installs?
[22:32] Rafael: yes, there's an on-prem package with offline bundles; need a longer lead time for that path.
[22:48] Ethan: can we stage a canary for rule changes? we want to test redaction rules on 5% traffic.
[22:55] Rafael: yes, rollout policies allow canary percentages and automatic revert on errors.
[23:10] [26:00] Maya: quick recap then next steps — raf, do you have the pilot checklist?
[23:18] Rafael: yes: 1) sample PII patterns from Paragon, 2) pilot route config (ephemeral/masked), 3) cost/latency baseline, 4) security pack review, 5) legal DPA sign-off.
[23:36] Lena: timeline question — can we start pilot by 2026-05-18?
[23:41] Maya: yes, assuming sample data and legal contact in the next week.
[23:47] Priya: final Q — what SLA for Dedicated vs hosted?
[23:52] Samir: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has standard uptime commitments. we'll include exact SLA numbers in the follow-up.
[24:05] Maya: i'm going to send the recording, security pack, and a small how-to for retention toggles. raf will share the API snippets.
[24:15] Ethan: thanks everyone, this is helpful.
[24:20] [End of meeting]
